{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=causal-guided+knowledge+editing+foundational+premises+evaluation&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"title\": [\"CAKE: Causal-Guided Adaptive Knowledge Editing for LLMs\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"title\": [\"Axioms and foundational premises\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2014, 1, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004\", \"title\": [\"Knowledge, Explanation, and Foundational Premises in Aristotle’s Posterior Analytics\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 11, 28]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7158698\", \"title\": [\"A Prior-Regularized Framework for Knowledge-Guided Differentiable Causal Discovery\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Purpose: Differentiable causal discovery methods ignore curated domain regulatory knowledge and underperform in high-dimensional, small-sample transcriptomic data. This Methodology paper proposes a universal prior-regularized computational framework that injects pairwise domain priors into gradient-based DAG learning for stable graph recovery in data-limited regimes. Methods: Prior-regularized causal discovery augments the NOTEARS objective with a penalty λ p ∥W-W prior ∥ 2 F , where W prior encodes pairwise interactions from TRRUST and STRING (combined score &gt; 900). The framework supports three backbones (NOTEARS, DAGMA, GOLEM). Validation includes DepMap CRISPR co-essentiality screening (1,208 genes × 18,531 cell lines) and GO enrichment (7,992 cancer-associated genes). Results: On synthetic Erdős-Rényi DAGs across six dimensions (d ∈ {30, 50, 80, 100, 150, 200}) with partial prior coverage (α ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7}), prior-regularized NOTEARS improves F1 in 15 of 24 configurations, with 98% relative gain at d = 30 (F1: 0.046 → 0.090) and a mean ∆F1 of 0.014 across all dimensions. The STRING prior achieves 100% coverage of TCGA cancer gene sets (mean 138 entries per d = 200 set, vs 21% for TRRUST). Consensus STRING analysis identifies TP53 (282 partners) and ribosomal ubiquitin proteins as dominant hubs anchoring prior-guided discovery. Conclusions: The framework enables causal discovery to leverage existing biological knowledge rather than rediscovering it, yielding the largest improvements where baseline performance is weakest. The methodology is database-agnostic, backbone-agnostic, fully reproducible, and applicable to any domain with curated pairwise knowledge.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7158698\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "d37d1e36fc2169baf5f6b69b376de3d38aab3244c7bfeee524a6271e78a902af", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918", "doi:10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006", "doi:10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7158698"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918", "https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006", "https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7158698"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=theoretical+models+of+intrinsic+motivation+and+objective+generation+in+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1\", \"title\": [\"Beyond Human-Designed Objectives: Autonomous Goal Generation in AI Through Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Directed Agency\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Current artificial intelligence systems remain fundamentally constrained by their dependence on human-designed objectives and reward functions, limiting their capacity for genuine autonomy and open-ended development. This paper proposes Autonomous Goal Generation Networks (AGGNs), a theoretical framework for architectures that synthesize, evaluate, and pursue their own objectives through intrinsic motivation. The framework specifies five components: Goal-Generative Networks (GGNs, based on a VAE-style sampler over a goal embedding space), Objective Evaluation Systems (OESs) with six explicit criteria, Intrinsic Motivation Engines (IMEs) implementing curiosity, competence, empowerment, autonomy, and aesthetic drives, Autonomous Agency Controllers (AACs) for concurrent-objective scheduling, and Self-Reflective Goal Refinement (SRGR) for closing the loop. We prove a goal-distribution convergence result (Theorem 1) under stationary feedback and a stability condition for the SRGR loop. The contribution of this paper is theoretical: we identify the structural and motivational ingredients an autonomously-goal-generating agent must possess. No empirical validation is reported.
